takeaway: Pus contains a mixture of dead and live neutrophils, plus fibrin, lipid, coagulation and complement factors.

question.text: A 47-year-old man has a 3 x 4 cm superficial abdominal wall abscess. Which statement regarding the pathology of abscesses is correct?
question.say: A 47-year-old man has a 3 by 4 centimetre superficial abdominal wall abscess. Which statement regarding the pathology of abscesses is correct?

answer.text: Pus contains a mixture of dead and live neutrophils.

lines.text: Here is the man with a small abscess on his abdominal wall.
Zoom in, and the cavity is full of pus.
Pus is not just bacteria. It holds fibrin, lipid, and coagulation and complement factors.
And it holds a mixture of neutrophils. Some are still alive and fighting.
Others are dead, lying in the pus.
lines.say: (laugh) Others are dead, lying in the pus.

lines.text: So pus has dead and live neutrophils. That is our answer.
A pilonidal abscess is usually colonised with coliforms, while a psoas abscess is most often caused by Staphylococcus aureus or tuberculosis.
